entities.summary: Ann Weldy, better known by her pen name Ann Bannon, is an American author who, from 1957 to 1962, wrote five lesbian pulp fiction novels known as The Beebo Brinker Chronicles. The books' enduring popularity and impact on lesbian identity has earned her the title "Queen of Lesbian Pulp Fiction". Bannon was a young housewife trying to address her own issues of sexuality when she was inspired to write her first novel. Her subsequent books featured four characters who reappeared throughout the series, including her eponymous heroine, Beebo Brinker, who came to embody the archetype of a butch lesbian.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ann Bannon's works had a significant impact on lesbian identity in North America during the mid-20th century, influencing generations of queer women and contributing to the development of feminist literature. Her novels remain popular today, with some estimates suggesting they have sold over 1 million copies.
